author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000002250 (PTHR48099)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel Nmdmc (Q04448)
Human MTHFD1L	 Q6UB35
Human MTHFD2   P13995

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
Mainly erroneous propagation, but there maybe an erroneous source too.


This node is annotated with this NADP-dependent catalytic term:
GO:0004488 methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase (NADP+) activity (EC:1.5.1.5)

However, some proteins in PTHR48099 are characterized to have the related, but different, NAD-dependent activity (e.g. Q04448):
GO:0004487 methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity (EC:1.5.1.15)

For humans, PTHR48099 includes:
MTHFD1	 P11586	C-1-tetrahydrofolate synthase, cytoplasmic 	= EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP)
MTHFD1L	 Q6UB35	Monofunctional C1-tetrahydrofolate synthase, mitochondrial 	= neither EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP) nor EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD)
MTHFD2	 P13995	Bifunctional methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase_cyclohydrolase, mitochondrial = EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD)
MTHFD2L 	 Q9H903	Bifunctional methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase_cyclohydrolase 2, mitochondrial 	= EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP) and EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD)
So annotating Q6UB35 and P13995 with the NADP-specific term looks incorrect.

(Note, MTHFD2 (P13995) does say "it can also utilize NADP at a reduced efficiency" and it is annotated with the NADP-dependent GO term (but not the EC number!) from PMID: 8218174 - however, that seems to be based on in vitro assays and the thrust of that paper is that it is a NAD-dependent enzyme)

So I think this node may need to be split?
title: PAINT issue: PTN000002250 (PTHR48099)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hello,
This is a big and complex family.
For MTHFD1 : EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP) - we are **correct**.
For MTHFD1L : neither EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP) nor EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD). -  **This looks correct too.** I do not see any annotation to GO:0004487 nor GO:0004488. This might have been changed recently ??
For MTHFD2 :  EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD) - We have annotation to both, **I've blocked annotation to NADP+**. We have both primary annotation in human and mouse.
For MTHFD2L : EC:1.5.1.5 (NADP) and EC:1.5.1.15 (NAD) We have only annotation to NADP+, since there is a mouse NOT primary annotation for NAD+ (the only sequence annotated in this node), I've blocked annotation to the node. I just **unblocked annotation to NAD+**.

In general I've removed annotation to GO:0004488 from the root and added it only to specific nodes.
I hope this resolves the issues.
I wonder if we need to be so specific when it comes to co-substrates. It seems to cause confusion at every level and isn't really reflected in the phylogenetic trees. Something to discuss...
Thanks,
Marc.

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks Marc. I think your changes will resolve the issue I reported.
(You're right about MTHFD1L - it was an error to have mentioned that in the original ticket.)
